title: Outcomes From Use of a Spinal Growth Guidance System in Early Onset Scoliosis
official: Post-approval Study to Evaluate the Safety and Efficacy of the VerteGlide Spinal Growth Guidance System for the Treatment of Early Onset Scoliosis (EOS)
summary:
This is a prospective, multicenter, observational study. The study will evaluate the long-term safety and performance of the VerteGlide Spinal Growth Guidance System in children with early-onset scoliosis (EOS).

All patients in the study will have blood collected during surgery to measure baseline metal ion levels. Patients will also have standardized follow-up visits. This information will help answer specific U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) questions about metal exposure in the body and additional surgeries after VerteGlide treatment.

Patients will be placed into one of two groups:

Asymptomatic Post-Operative Cohort: Patients who do not have symptoms that require another surgery.

Subsequent Surgical Intervention (SSI) Cohort: Patients who have a planned or unplanned additional surgery.

During the study, some patients may move from the Asymptomatic Post-Operative Cohort to the SSI Cohort if they need another surgery.

Before any study-specific procedures are performed, informed consent will be obtained from the patient's parent or legal guardian. The patient will also provide assent when appropriate.

The study is designed to follow the usual care for children with EOS as much as possible. This will reduce extra visits and procedures for patients and their families and may help patients remain in the study.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

1. Diagnosis of EOS and will be treated with the VerteGlide system in accordance with the approved indications for use.
2. Subject will be less than 10 years of age at the date of the index (initial) surgery.
3. Written informed consent obtained from a legally authorized representative (and subject assent, as applicable).
4. Subject and/or representative demonstrate an understanding of the study requirements and a willingness to comply with all scheduled follow-up procedures.

Exclusion Criteria:

1. Documented or suspected material allergy or intolerance, specifically to Ti-6Al-4V, Titanium, and Cobalt.
2. A metal implant (or metal component) in situ.
3. Known inadequate bone strength for secure device fixation.
4. Active systemic infection or infection localized to the intended implant site.
5. Any active systemic disease (including malignancy) that, in the opinion of the Investigator, would compromise the subject's welfare or the overall integrity and outcome of the study.
6. Inadequate soft tissue coverage over the operative site.
7. Implant components would be too large or too small for the subject.
8. Any patient in which implant utilization would interfere with anatomical structures or expected physiologic performance.
9. Presence of any condition that produces loads on the device that could lead to failure (e.g., obesity).
10. Spinal cord abnormalities that require treatment.
11. Absent diaphragmatic function
12. Previous spine surgery that would confound VerteGlide outcomes.
13. Inability or unwillingness to follow a post-operative regimen or scheduled study procedures.
